# BSC (Bharat Steel Group) — Sales Call Knowledge Base (auto-distilled)

## Corpus summary

This corpus is a large mixed batch of call recordings, but only a modest fraction qualify as genuine **sales** conversations (rate enquiries, quotations, order confirmation, dispatch/payment-for-material talk, dealer/distributor negotiation). A very large share of the dump is **not usable** for sales training:

- Dozens of calls are pure **internal production/operator chatter** (the "Yuvraj Operator" series — coil cutting, plate diagonal checks, sheet thickness, loading/unloading instructions) — operational, not sales.
- Many calls are **personal/unrelated** (the long Hindi/Gujarati "Vishal" calls about cricket teams, family, silver/gold market chit-chat, WhatsApp photos) — not company sales calls at all.
- Several are **transport/logistics negotiations** with truck/vehicle brokers (Dushyant/Vizag transporters) — freight rate haggling, not product sales to end customers.
- A good number are **voicemails, wrong numbers, one-line calls, or disconnected/garbled audio**.

The **real sales signal** comes from a recurring set of calls with structural steel / TMT / plate customers (fabricators, contractors, traders, builders) — covering stock/rate enquiries, quotation negotiation, cutting/size customization, part-payment/credit terms, delivery/transport charge disputes, and billing/documentation friction. This KB is built strictly from those calls. Given the noise ratio, conclusions below are kept close to what is explicitly said — no invented SKUs, prices, or policies.

## Products & brand ladder

From real sales talk, BSC deals in **structural & flat steel products**, not roofing:

- **TMT bars / rebar** — grades mentioned: **Fe500, Fe500D, Fe550D**. One call clarifies: *"500D தான் sir வரும் CRS-ல... 550 வராது sir sale-ல 500D தான் manufacture ஆகும்"* [Only 500D is made in sale/CRS category, not 550]. Brands referenced: **Vizag (RINL)**, **Sail**, **JSW**, **Vaisakh**. Lengths standard at 12m; one customer wanted thread-rolling (bolt use) and asked for 3m-cut pieces — BSC explicitly does **not cut TMT**: *"TMT-ல நம்ம 6 meter எப்பவுமே கொடுக்கலையே"* [We never give 6m in TMT].
- **Structural sections**: ISMB, ISA (L-angle), C-channel, I-channel, square/rectangular pipe, SHS. One customer clarifies: *"SHS நம்ம deal பண்றது இல்ல sir. மத்த item-லாம் குடுக்குறோம்"* [We don't deal SHS, we supply the other items].
- **MS Plates / sheets (CR/HR)** — thicknesses from 2mm to 45mm+, sizes like 4x8, 8x20, 2500x6300mm coils; "checkered plate" also mentioned. Cut-to-size service exists for plates (*"size வாங்கினா நாங்க cut பண்ணிக்கலாம்"*) but **not for angles/flats** (*"Flats-லாம் நம்ம cut பண்றது கிடையாது"*).
- **Flats / MS flat bars** — e.g., 50x5, 100x6mm.
- **CRS (Cold Rolled Sections)** — limited item range confirmed by staff: *"நம்மகிட்ட நம்மகிட்ட இது ஒரே ஒரு item தான் இருக்கு"* [We only have one item in stock] for 20mm CRS; CR coldrolled sheet (0.6mm, IS 513 grade) sourced via referral, not directly stocked.
- Brand-grade note: **Vaisakh and Sale(Sail)** are priced the same (*"ரெண்டுமே same price தான்"*), but customers sometimes explicitly reject one brand for another.

## Real rates & terms (only rates that actually appear in the calls)

Rates are **highly date/market dependent** (steel price fluctuates daily) — reps repeatedly quote "today's rate" rather than fixed price lists:

- TMT 12mm: **₹69/kg**, 16mm: **₹68.5/kg** (+GST extra, not inclusive) — quoted to Saveetha Institute.
- Plate rates seen across calls: **₹61–₹67/kg** range depending on thickness (2mm ≈ ₹63, 3–5mm ≈ ₹61–61.5, 6mm ≈ ₹66–67, 8mm ≈ ₹67).
- TMT/structural "Vizag" wholesale rates quoted around **₹62,000–₹65,000/ton** depending on size slab (16–25mm ≈ 65, 12mm ≈ 67, 10mm ≈ 68–69, 8mm ≈ 70) in one builder call — showing a **thickness-based price ladder, thinner sizes cost more**.
- CRS 20mm: **₹69,000** (including plus loading, but loading **can be waived**: *"loading free பண்ணலாம் ஒன்னும் problem இல்ல"*).
- Sample policy: 1-meter / 1-piece free sample given for customer testing, but **customer must collect themselves**: *"1 meter-க்கு 1 piece தான் sir குடுப்போம்... நீங்கதான் வந்து இங்க வந்து collect பண்ணனும்"*.
- Payment/handling charge: a recurring **"₹200 standard" payment/handling charge** per vehicle is mentioned in two separate disputes — customers complain it was suddenly raised to ₹250 without notice; BSC staff maintain it's vehicle-capacity based, not arbitrary, and offer to raise it with MD/escalate.
- Transport: trailer (40ft) movement rates quoted around **₹15,000** (customer side, Sangeetha Traders), BSC->customer freight examples: Thiruvallur/Gudur ≈ ₹18/ton-based, Trichy-Thoothukudi ≈ ₹1800 for 15–16 ton.
- Credit: standard credit mentioned is **1 month** (*"1 month தான். credit"*); advance/credit customers get a **slightly higher rate than advance-payment customers** — confirmed explicitly: *"like என்னோட rate-ல இருந்து கரெக்டா இருந்தது advance payment கரெக்டா இருந்தது credit-னா கொஞ்சம் இது"*.
- Discounts given only on bulk/committed orders (e.g., ₹500/ton or ₹1/kg shaved off when matching competitor rate from "Kapil").
- Full payment generally required before load/dispatch (cash-and-carry norm) — "Cash and Carry தான் நான் எல்லாருக்குமே கொடுத்துருக்கேன்."

## Objection Playbook

**1. "Your rate is higher than competitor X"**
- Rep holds firm on correctness of rate rather than conceding immediately: *"கரெக்டா இருக்கு rate Sir. correct rate கொடுத்திருக்கேன்."*
- When pushed, reps may offer a marginal reduction only after checking with seniors/supplier ("Kapil sir கிட்ட கேட்டு வேணா சொல்றேன்").

**2. "You increased loading/handling charges suddenly without notice"**
- This is the single most repeated objection in the corpus (two long calls). Rep response pattern: acknowledge standard ₹200 charge exists, blame billing-team/vehicle-capacity logic, avoid admitting fault, and push to escalate/discuss with MD rather than refund unilaterally: *"நான் debit note raise பண்ணிடுறேன் உங்களுக்கு."*
- Lesson: **never let vehicle/loading-charge disputes drag on call-to-call** — standardize and communicate upfront.

**3. "Payment proof / weighment slip is incomplete (no photo, no vehicle number)"**
- Customer insists on proper documentation before accepting discrepancy; rep initially blames "camera/system problem," customer rejects excuse: *"நீங்க payment இல்லைங்க excuse சொல்லாதீங்க."*
- Resolution offered: reprint with seal and signature.

**4. "Price is very high right now, should I buy less?"**
- Good proactive-advisory selling observed: rep **advises customer to buy only what's urgently needed**, not to over-stock at high prices, promising price may fall in 2–3 days: *"ரொம்ப வாங்காதீங்க... Suppose உங்களுக்கு ஒரு 5 ton தேவன்னா அது மட்டும் வாங்குங்க."* This builds trust even though it reduces immediate order size.

**5. "Can you cut this to a smaller length?"**
- For flats/angles: firmly declined (cutting not offered; extra transport suggested instead). For plates: cutting is offered as a value-add.

**6. New/small customers asking for small quantities**
- Policy stated: *"New customer-க்கு எல்லாம் சின்ன சின்ன quantity குடுக்குறது இல்ல sir"* — small/trial orders are discouraged for unknown customers; distributor channel used for small quantities instead.

**7. Billing/GST/address mismatches**
- Common friction point — customers often need billing address, GST number, or shipping address changed last-minute; reps handle via WhatsApp confirmation before dispatch, and generally refuse to alter an already-issued e-invoice/e-way bill once generated.

## Effective Lines (openings, discovery, closing, follow-up)

**Opening / identification**
- *"Hello Sir, [Company name]-ல இருந்து பேசுறேன்."* — immediate self + company identification is universal and expected.
- *"Sir, good morning. rate என்ன போகுது?"* — casual rate-check opener used daily by repeat B2B buyers (fabricators/traders).

**Discovery**
- *"என்ன size வேணும் sir? எவ்வளவு quantity வேணும்?"* — always clarify size + quantity before quoting.
- *"Delivery location எங்க?"* — location clarified early since it affects transport-inclusive vs ex-works pricing.
- *"Brand எது வேணும்? Sale-ஆ, Vaisakh-ஆ?"* — brand preference probed since multiple mills are stocked.

**Pricing framing**
- *"இது wholesale rate. நீங்க என்ன எதிர்பார்க்கிறீங்க சொல்லுங்க."* — effective reframe to invite a concrete counter rather than open-ended bargaining.
- *"ex-work rate குடுத்துறேன் நீங்க mail அனுப்புங்க."* — separates material price from logistics cleanly.

**Urgency/closing**
- *"Okay-ன்னா நான் PO அனுப்பிச்சிடுறேன்."* — natural close once price agreed.
- *"நான் order கண்டிப்பா எடுப்பேன், அதனாலதான் சொல்றேன்"* (dealer/distributor to BSC) — reciprocity framing to extract a better rate before committing.
- Zetwork call: rep stalls firmly but constructively — *"நீங்க 10 minutes எடுங்க 15 minutes எடுங்க no issue"* — gives customer room to negotiate internally without losing the thread.
